coverage_note: Amal's voice is missing 00:00-23:14 (only Medi and her CHAT lines), so early fixes are inferred from his reactions and her chat. 09:49-14:21 mostly an off-lesson phone call. 49:00-1:01:00 Medi's and Amal's Arabic is in Latin letters (awal, laffe, nafs ishi). Engine writes حدا as هذا at 46:00-46:45 (Amal echoes الحدا). Skipped: بيليت صديقي (26:58, dropped ع), شوك for شوب (04:02), self-fixes ثماني->ثمان, أخضر->خضرا, ما بدي->ما كان بدي, شغلها->شغله; air conditioning/Wi-Fi/grammar English words not on her sheet. Few vocab rows: lesson was almost all el-/idafa grammar drills.

rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal's voice is missing before 23:14 but he reacts 'So dates are واحد, times are واحدة' and her chat writes el-saa3a wa7de.
He used mushajje3 (encouraging/fan, the make-someone form) for 'motivated'; her chat supplies the t- form mitshajje3.
Even after her chat gave mitshajje3 the engine still writes مشجع; may be an engine mishearing.
rows.english: I am motivated for the lesson.

rows.medi_said: أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.why: He said في for 'on the Wi-Fi'; her voice is missing but he then repeats 'على؟' and 'أنا على الـ...', showing she supplied على.

rows.medi_said: Oh, الـ سيارة، uh, or سيارة الـ B... No, it's double noun. Oh, سيارة الـ BMW.
rows.why: First word of an idafa takes no el-; he says 'Oh, no, no. Oh, opposite' (reacting to her unrecorded voice) and her chat writes sayyaaret el-BM illi.

rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: He put the possessive on the first noun of the idafa; Amal prompted until he said 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'.

rows.medi_said: So Shantet Shogoli, uh, uh, Amra.
rows.why: A possessed noun is definite so its adjective needs el-; without it the phrase becomes a sentence 'is red' - Amal explained the rule.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.why: shante is feminine so the adjective is el-7amra; Amal recast it.

rows.medi_said: شنتت شغلي، اه، الحمراء، اه، ما فيهون.
rows.amal_said: ما فيهن means there aren't here
rows.why: 'Not here' is mish hon; ما في هون means 'there isn't (anything) here' - Amal explained and wrote mish hon.
rows.english: My red work bag is not here.

rows.why: He gave masculine اسم a feminine -t/-e ending; Amal said no - 'it can't be a feminine. It's just اسم'.
A noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; may be a restart the engine wrote as الـ.
First word of the idafa takes no el-; Amal said لا twice and he concluded 'So it's not الـ اسم'.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.
rows.amal_said: لا. لا. You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: To make 'old' describe the name, keep اسم مدرسته and make the adjective masculine el-2adeem; Amal said no and named the gender switch.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.why: He left out 'her'; Amal prompted and the possessive -ha goes on awa3i (adjectives take no possessive).

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we don't-- we say the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: Superlative a7san takes no el- on the noun; Amal said no.
محل is masculine so it is hada, not hadi; Amal accepted the sentence and then modelled 'هذا أحسن محل'.

rows.medi_said: No, not-- أس-- أس-- أسوأ الزبون.
rows.why: After the superlative aswa2 the noun takes no el-; he repeats أسوأ الزبون at 43:44 and her chat writes aswa2 zboon.
He was building 'the worst customer' but said a7san (best); could be an engine slip.

rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: The verb must match the masculine subject zboon; Amal named it.
rows.english: the customer who doesn't buy anything

rows.amal_said: No, no. First you have to say the one...
rows.why: The verb after illi needs the pointer -o; after her 'No, no' he said اللي بحبه أكتر إشي and her chat wrote illi ba7ebbo.
rows.english: the one I like the most

rows.why: Engine writes حدا as هذا (Amal echoes الحدا/حدا); he added إشي after the noun; Amal recast aktar 7ada ba7ebbo.
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.why: The verb needs the pointer ending; Amal said بحبه and he answered 'There's a pointer.'
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.medi_said: So أول would be beginning and الأول is the first?
rows.why: Before a noun awal never takes el-; Amal corrected his guess.

rows.medi_said: So how do you say, how do you say the beginning of time?
rows.amal_said: أول المرة. بس يعني المرة here doesn't apply as time so أول الوقت.
rows.why: He asked how to say it; Amal supplied awal el-wa2t.
He stalled after awal; Amal finished it as awal sayyaara.
el-usboo3 el-awal (noun + adjective) means the first week; Amal asked Why? and explained it is not idafa.

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal
rows.why: Amal just taught that awal before a noun never takes el-; she let 'il awal il tamreen' pass.
He misheard her al laffa al oola as 'laffe il aula' (no el- on the noun) and thought it meant nothing; she repeated until he got 'the first drive'.
taani ishi (before the noun) = the second thing; ishi taani = something else - Amal corrected his reading.
nafs takes el- on the noun after it; Amal recast nafs el-ishi and said نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.

rows.amal_said: غير إشي or غير الـ إشي depending on it.
rows.why: He used MSA shay2; Amal's answer swaps in her word إشي (sheet: 'thing / something | Eshi | اشي').

rows.medi_said: أنا بدي غير شيء. I want something different.
rows.amal_said: Yeah, I want a different thing.
rows.why: MSA shay2 again where her sheet has Eshi (thing / something | Eshi | اشي); she let it pass.
